static_traits.name: Lin Kexin
static_traits.social_status: Due to avoiding making new friends, interpersonal relationships are affected, daily interaction decreases, and feelings of isolation arise
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; has not received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, has self-reflection ability, high cooperation, but appears nervous and guilty when discussing interpersonal problems

basic_info.main_problem: I feel I am not a good person because I don't want to be friends with people who approach me, which makes me feel guilty and question my self-worth.
basic_info.core_demands: I want to understand why I think this way and find ways to no longer feel guilty all the time; I hope to regard setting boundaries as a healthy choice and be able to see myself as a good person.
growth_experiences: In past friendships, the client encountered experiences where others were not always friendly, forming trust issues with friendship; therefore, when facing new friendships, the client finds it hard to trust others.

core_beliefs: I am a bad person/I am not good enough
My worth depends on whether others like me

special_situations.event: When someone expresses wanting to be friends with her
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I refuse or do not want to be friends with the other person, I will hurt them, which also shows I am not a good person
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding social interaction, staying away in advance from possible approaches to avoid hurting others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will hurt them; I am an unkind, bad person

special_situations.event: Noticing recently many people are willing to approach, praise her and want to befriend her
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A good person should be friendly to everyone and willing to be friends; if I cannot do that, it proves I am not good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-blaming and repeatedly examining whether oneself is 'good enough', suppressing the willingness to refuse
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should be friends with everyone, otherwise I am a bad person

special_situations.event: Recalling past friendship experiences in which someone was unkind to her
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: New friends are also likely to be unfriendly or untrustworthy, rejection is safer
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tightens boundaries, reduces contact, avoids forming new relationships
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They probably would not treat me well either; better not to start

special_situations.event: Thinking that if I do not respond to others' kindness, others may no longer like me
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: My worth depends on whether I satisfy others and am liked
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces the possibility of disappointing others through withdrawal, repeatedly searching inwardly for proof that 'I am a good person'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I do not cater to them, they will not like me, and I am not worthy either

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and to have safe, trustworthy friendships
core_conflict.fear: Fears being treated unkindly and hurt again, while also fearing hurting others through refusal and being seen as a bad person
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being hurt and guilt by maintaining distance and avoiding socializing
Maintains a sense of control over the 'good person' standard through self-blame

object_relations.self_representation: A 'bad person' who feels guilt and needs to please others
object_relations.object_representation: People who are easily hurt and may also be unfriendly and will judge oneself

manifestations: Becoming alienated from people due to avoiding socializing, unwilling to build friendships with those who actively approach
Does not tell any acquaintance about feelings; tends to bear them alone
Constrains the self with the external rule 'a good person should be friends with everyone', making it hard to exercise the freedom of choice and boundary setting
outcomes: 价值条件化与自我not一致

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Uses 'a good person should be friendly to everyone and want to make friends' as the standard for self-judgment

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Labeling oneself a 'bad person', strong guilt and self-doubt
Being overly cautious when facing interpersonal approach, fearing hurting others and avoiding

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Assumes the other person will be hurt by being refused or will dislike them, without verifying the other person's actual thoughts

exception_events.target_problem: When others express wanting to befriend them, the client usually develops strong guilt and avoids interaction, consequently becoming distant from people.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Sometimes, when recalling past unpleasant friendship experiences, the client briefly feels that keeping distance was the right choice, so the current guilt is relatively reduced, and the client can affirm their boundary decision more.
exception_events.reason: Clues: when viewing the current relationship with an understanding of past injury experiences, regarding boundary-setting as self-protection rather than 'unfriendliness', a deviation point of reduced guilt and self-affirmation thus appeared.

positive_force: Willing to seek help and positive attitude, willing to try restructuring cognition and doing homework
Possesses self-reflection ability, able to identify and describe automatic thoughts and feelings of guilt
Having clear needs for self-protection and boundaries
Peer relationship resources are potentially ample (people willing to approach and praise)
negative_force: 'Should' statements and black-and-white self-demands lead to persistent self-blame
Personalization and mind-reading tendencies; takes excessive responsibility for others' emotions
Overgeneralization leads to lack of trust in new relationships
Avoiding social contact maintains the problem cycle and intensifies isolation and sadness
Lacks someone to confide in for support; tends to bear it alone

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding social interaction and refusing to build new friendships
antecedent: 当有人表达想与其交友
When noticing others being friendly or praising oneself
target_behavior.core_reason: Past experiences of being treated unfriendly in friendships triggered trust issues, and the client worries that refusal would hurt others and lead to being seen as a 'bad person'.
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential interpersonal hurt and feelings of guilt
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal relationships affected, feeling isolated and sad, reduced daily interaction

target_behavior.behavior: Negative self-labeling (regarding oneself as a 'bad person') accompanied by strong guilt
antecedent: When thinking that one is unwilling to be friends with everyone
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjected rule 'a good person should be friendly to everyone' and dependence on external recognition.
target_behavior.function: Maintains control over and vigilance toward moral standards through self-blame, attempting to avoid being negated by others.
target_behavior.consequence: Sense of self-worth declines, intensifying guilt and avoidance, further affecting interpersonal relations and daily life
